description: The white silk áo dài of a high-school girl: a long fitted tunic split to the waist over loose white trousers.  Every morning the streets filled with them, flowing behind bicycles.
A festive red silk áo dài embroidered with gold phoenixes, worn for Tết and weddings over white trousers.
A thin, faded cotton t-shirt from a market stall, printed with a cartoon and a slogan in broken English.
Dark polyester office slacks with a sharp crease, worn by clerks, teachers and every man going somewhere respectable.
Áo khoác chống nắng: a thin, hooded pastel jacket with long sleeves and thumb loops, worn by women on motorbikes to keep their skin pale.  It covers everything except the eyes.
Nón kết: a cheap baseball cap with a crooked peak and a fake brand logo stitched on the front.
Dép lào: thick rubber sandals with a strap over the toes and another around the heel, nearly indestructible.  Soldiers, farmers and xe ôm drivers have walked a long way in them.
The khaki-yellow shirt of a ward police officer, with red collar tabs and shoulder boards.  The badge has been torn off.
Olive-green uniform trousers from a ward police or militia uniform.
A short-sleeved white school shirt with the school's name embroidered in blue over the pocket.
Khăn quàng đỏ: the red triangular neckerchief of the Young Pioneers, knotted at the throat of every primary-school child.
